Categories.value: Taken with Canon EOS 5D Mark IV and Canon EF 11-24mm F4L USM|Amantaka Hotel|Self-published work|Bathrooms in Laos|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Hotels photographed in 2023|Photographs by Basile Morin|Symmetry impressions of building interiors|Laos photographs taken on 2023-09-18|Long exposure photography in architecture|Vertical symmetry impressions|Bathroom mirrors

ImageDescription.value: Bathroom of Khan Pool Suite in Amantaka luxury resort and hotel in Luang Prabang, Laos. Amantaka is one of the 34 properties operated by Aman Resorts, hospitality company founded by Indonesian hotelier Adrian Zecha in 1988, present in more than 20 countries. The hotel, located in a French colonial building, opened in September 2009. A boutique hotel, it contains 24 lavish suites, encircling a central courtyard and is designed with a mixture of traditional Lao furnishings and modern. The suites range in size from 70 to 120 square metres and include eight suites, four pool suites, eight Khan pool suites, two Mekong pool suites and two Amantaka pool suites. All of the rooms have a king-sized bed centre of the suites beneath a traditional high ceiling. They are painted in white and have mahogany or dark wood furnishings and windows. The rooms are reported to be between 1,100 USD and 1,900 USD a night, the most expensive being the Amantaka pool suites (1,900 USD).

A boutique hotel, it contains 24 lavish suites, encircling a central courtyard and is designed with a mixture of traditional Lao furnishings and modern. The suites range in size from 70 to 120 square metres and include eight suites, four pool suites, eight Khan pool suites, two Mekong pool suites and two Amantaka pool suites. All of the rooms have a king-sized bed centre of the suites beneath a traditional high ceiling. They are painted in white and have mahogany or dark wood furnishings and windows. The rooms are reported to be between 1,100 USD and 1,900 USD a night.
